title: Browser-control surface discovery before owner handoff
owner_outcome: Use the available browser-control capability directly and avoid asking the owner to perform browser steps that Chat can perform itself.
observed_failure: A remote-shell xdg-open failure was interpreted too broadly even though other browser-control surfaces were available.
causal_mechanism: The execution surface was misclassified: shell process control was treated as equivalent to the user's graphical browser-control surface, and no current-turn browser-surface discovery check ran before owner escalation.
normalized_rule: Before browser or GUI work, discover the current Chat browser/computer-control surfaces. Do not infer browser unavailability from xdg-open/open/start failure in a remote or non-GUI shell. Use an authorized browser-control surface for all automatable steps and ask the owner only for an irreducible human authentication/consent gesture.
enforcement: Root AGENTS.md browser-control efficiency section carries the rule on every governed turn.
A focused regression test requires explicit browser-surface discovery, shell/GUI distinction, launcher-failure non-equivalence, and minimal human-gate handoff.
scope: Portable browser-control routing and owner-interruption behavior; does not bypass authentication, consent, CAPTCHA, passkey, or other genuinely human-only gates.
